title: Fair-share batch scheduler with KV-reservation and SLO-aware eviction
creator: Samir Patel
description:
Problem: under mixed-tenant continuous batching workloads we see two linked failure modes: (1) aggressive tenants dominate GPU memory and KV residency which causes tail latency regressions for latency-sensitive tenants, and (2) coarse-grained preemption triggers full KV cache thrashing leading to repeated warmups and higher per-token cost. Existing preemption policies are either too blunt (evict entire KV working sets) or too conservative (allow popular tenants to starve SLO-sensitive traffic).

Goal: implement a fair-share batch scheduler that combines soft KV-reservations, SLO-aware admission, and memory-aware batch shaping to: (a) preserve P99 latency targets for latency-tier tenants, (b) limit unnecessary KV evictions, and (c) improve average GPU memory utilization without increasing error rates.

Proposed approach summary: a) Fair-share tokens: assign per-tenant admission tokens proportional to tenant weight/SLO tier. Tokens gate batch admission into latency-critical fast-paths. b) KV-reservation slices: allocate a small, elastic KV-reservation quota per tenant (measured in entries or MB) that prevents single-tenant eviction storms; reservations are reclaimed on sustained low activity. c) Soft preemption: on memory pressure, instead of immediate KV evictions for the next request, the scheduler applies a graded admission delay (micro-sleep + priority bump) to long-running/low-priority requests to allow short latency requests to complete. d) Memory-aware batch shaping: batch formation considers per-request peak memory estimate (from profile table) and will carve mixed batches to avoid surpassing per-GPU budgets and to reduce cross-tenant KV mixing. e) Adaptive eviction thresholds: eviction aggressiveness is tuned by request mix signals (tail SLO breaches increase conservatism).

Why different from existing policies: this ticket focuses on combining lightweight KV reservations (not hard partitions), proportional fairness via tokens, and soft micro-preemption (delay/band reduction) rather than immediate eviction. It explicitly targets reducing KV warmup cost and improving steady-state tail latency without sacrificing utilization.

Constraints and non-goals: we will not implement full working-set partitioning (hard tenant isolation) in this scope; we will not change the core kernel selection logic except to add minor per-batch memory heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: Under synthetic mixed workload (70% throughput, 30% latency SLO tenants) p99 latency for latency-tier tenants <= 1.5x baseline SLO for 95% of runs
KV eviction churn (MB evicted per 10k tokens) reduced by >= 30% compared to current preemptor under the same load scenario
GPU memory utilization more stable: <10% variance in 95th percentile across tenants vs current baseline
No increase in error rate / OOMs in dedicated e2e test cluster
Unit + integration test coverage for token accounting, KV-reservation lifecycle, and soft preemption path merged and passing CI
testing_plan:
1) Unit tests for token counter, reservation reclaiming, and eviction heuristics. 2) Microbench: run mixed synthetic tenant generator (latency + throughput profiles) against local dev cluster with instrumentation to measure p50/p95/p99, KV eviction MB, and memory variance. 3) Staging run in dedicated e2e cluster for 72h with production-like load generator. 4) Canary rollout: enable feature flag on 10% of nodes for dedicated customers with telemetry.

Test artifacts: benchmark dashboards (link below) and a harness script in /bench/ksim.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature-gated opt-in in dev for validation. Phase 1: enable on staging with synthetic load and enable detailed tracing. Phase 2: canary to 10% of dedicated pool (low-risk tenants) for 48h. Phase 3: 50% rollout with rollback guard rails (auto-disable on p99 regression > 2x or KV eviction surge > 2x). Phase 4: full rollout and retrospective.
metrics: Admission token queue length and wait time
